description: Buff-state outline presets: emissive color, scale and fade times applied to character/weapon or shikigami materials when status bits turn on/off.

ID.simple: Outline preset key (BREAK_FALL, INVINCIBLE, SUPER_ARMOR, HYPER_ARMOR, LIMITLESS, COUNTER).
ID.technical: FName (declared Id, export key ID) used as the DataTable row name; consumers pass a name to FindRow rather than reading Row->Id, although every exported ID value matches its row name. Shikigami_FindMaterialOutlineRow walks MaterialOutlineDataTables (+0x810, retail VA 0x14126A9E0) in array order and returns the first FindRow hit. The outline callers pass bCheckNone=false and bWarn=false but guard NAME_None themselves, so a missing row silently produces no animation. AGameCharacter::Tick gates on bOutlineEnabled and derives six bits from status/action queries (battle-sequence playback forces all zero), assigning AddOutline/RemoveOutline in the order LIMITLESS (0x1), COUNTER (0x2), BREAK_FALL (0x4), SUPER_ARMOR (0x8), HYPER_ARMOR (0x10), INVINCIBLE (0x20). AGameShikigami::Tick also gates on bOutlineEnabled and requests only INVINCIBLE when collision-lock membership changes for lock 4 or 5.

OutlineEmissiveColor.technical: Declared FVector (UE5 three doubles); the explicit FLinearColor conversion copies X,Y,Z to R,G,B and sets A=1. The float values are handed unchanged to StartOutlineEmissiveColor, so values above 1 are not clamped by this code (LIMITLESS Z=2.6; SUPER_ARMOR/HYPER_ARMOR/COUNTER X=1.1/1.1/1.5). Characters pass the same color to the body MaterialController and through WeaponController to each weapon; shikigami pass it to their MaterialController. Exact exported RGB: BREAK_FALL (0,1,0), INVINCIBLE (0.6,0.6,0.9), SUPER_ARMOR (1.1,0.8,0), HYPER_ARMOR (1.1,0,0), LIMITLESS (1.2,0,2.6), COUNTER (1.5,0.6,0.3); the constructor default is ZeroVector.

OutlineScale.technical: Declared float at layout offset +0x28 (constructor default 0.0). It is passed as the Goal to StartOutlineScale for every cached OutlineScale animator on the character body, each weapon, and (for shikigami) the shikigami material controller; the Duration is the same row FadeInTime. Exported values: 3.0 for BREAK_FALL and INVINCIBLE; 4.0 for SUPER_ARMOR, HYPER_ARMOR, LIMITLESS and COUNTER. The animator writes the interpolated value to the cached OutlineScale scalar parameter of each material instance while its tween is active.

FadeInTime.technical: Declared float seconds at layout offset +0x2C (constructor default 0.0). Used as Duration for both StartOutlineEmissiveColor and StartOutlineScale on the add path. StartTo begins a linear tween from each parameter's captured material default to the row Goal, advanced by controller DeltaSeconds; Duration <= 0 also applies the Goal immediately. Exported values are 0 for BREAK_FALL, INVINCIBLE and COUNTER and 0.05 s for SUPER_ARMOR, HYPER_ARMOR and LIMITLESS.

FadeOutTime.simple: Duration of the outline reset when the buff turns off.
FadeOutTime.technical: Declared float seconds at layout offset +0x30 (constructor default 0.0). Read only when a previously displayed buff bit turns off and no add name was selected; it is passed to AGameCharacter::ResetOutline or AGameShikigami::ResetOutline, which reset both cached Outline* parameter animators to the defaults captured from their material instances over this duration. Row color and scale are not read on removal. Duration <= 0 applies those defaults immediately; all six exported rows set 0.0. SetOutlineEnabled(false) bypasses this row path and resets with 0.0 directly.

notes: MaterialOutlineDataTables is manager slot +0x810. "MaterialOutlineDataTable" is registered as a primary-asset loader name (GameDataTableManager.cpp:432); after all loaders complete, Tick resolves that one asset into the array (line 259). The shared finder iterates the array in order, so with the exported data there is one source table; duplicate keys, if introduced, would resolve to the first match.

The character assigns one AddOutline/RemoveOutline name while testing the six bits in ascending order LIMITLESS, COUNTER, BREAK_FALL, SUPER_ARMOR, HYPER_ARMOR, INVINCIBLE; later active (or removed) bits overwrite earlier ones. If both an add and a removal are produced in the same tick, the AddOutline branch runs and the removal is ignored. Battle-sequence playback forces the new bit set to zero; the character INVINCIBLE bit uses collision locks 5/6/9, the shikigami uses locks 4/5, and both ticks are gated by bOutlineEnabled.

The material controllers create MIDs for each mesh material and, when OutlineEmissiveColor/OutlineScale exist, initialize animators with the parameter index and current/default value (GameCharacterMaterialController.cpp:159-172; GameShikigamiMaterialController.cpp:26-38; GameWeaponMaterialController.cpp:102-115). Start*/Reset* enqueue those animators; TickMaterialAnimators advances them and writes SetVectorParameterByIndex/SetScalarParameterByIndex (GameMaterialParameterAnimator.h:57-72, 122-133). This establishes the destination parameters and the reset target; the row-to-parameter binding is made only through the Start*/ResetOutline call sites.
This is a separate table from MaterialRimDataTable (+0x820), which has no identified row consumer in the available source.

Evidence boundary: all runtime statements above come from the reconstructed C++ sources (the shared row finder at 0x126a9e0 is behaviour-certified, not a byte-match) plus the single export. No retail Blueprint graph/asset evidence was available; the project guide states retail Blueprints contain no logic, so no Blueprint-level behavior is claimed.

usages.detail: Shikigami_FindMaterialOutlineRow walks MaterialOutlineDataTables and returns the first row with the requested name; outline callers pass bCheckNone=false and bWarn=false (retail finder 0x126a9e0).
After all primary-asset loads complete, GameDataTableManager resolves MaterialOutlineDataTable into MaterialOutlineDataTables (+0x810); this array is the only alias the finder consults.
Character tick maps six status/action bits to LIMITLESS/COUNTER/BREAK_FALL/SUPER_ARMOR/HYPER_ARMOR/INVINCIBLE row requests in precedence order; add wins over removal.
Adds the row's color/scale over FadeInTime to the body and every weapon material controller; the otherwise exclusive removal branch resets them over FadeOutTime.
Shikigami tick requests INVINCIBLE on a change in collision locks 4/5 and uses the same four row fields on its material controller.
StartTo/ResetToDefault drive linear tweens from captured material defaults; nonpositive durations apply immediately and Tick writes the cached MID parameter indices.
